html:
Tahitian pearls are dark pearls grown in the black-lip pearl oyster in the lagoons of French Polynesia. Pearl farming began in the 1960s, on atolls of the Tuamotu such as Manihi.

Polynesians had long dived for wild pearl shell, which traders bought in the 19th century for buttons; see pearl hunting. Overfishing nearly wiped out wild stocks, and farming replaced diving.

From the 1980s the pearls became the territory's largest export, earning more than anything but tourism. They gave work on remote atolls when the test centre was winding down, though prices fell sharply in the 2000s. See also French Polynesia.
